text: Milestone. My first podium was the biggest milestone.
Podium. He has been on the podium four times.
Club. I have been in the same club since I was nine.
Trophy. The trophy is still on the shelf.
Coach. My coach has known me for six years.
Junior. He has been in the junior category since last year.
Season. The season starts in March.
Teammate. My teammate has been surfing longer than me.
I have surfed since I was eight.
He has been in the club for six seasons.
Since when? For how long?
I have been surfing since I was eight.
I have been in the same club for six years.
How long have you been doing that?
Since when?
I have not been in the water since Sunday.

I have been coaching at this club for nineteen years, and I have seen a lot of kids come through. Most of them stay for one season. He has been with me since he was nine, which is unusual. What I tell parents is always the same thing: nothing happens in the first two years. Nothing. He finished last in his first four events and he did not miss a single training session. Then at fourteen, the podium. People say it happened suddenly. It has been happening slowly since he was nine, and nobody was watching.

We have been teammates since primary school, so about seven years. I have known him longer than anybody at that club except the coach. Honestly, he was not the best one when we started. There were four of us and he was the slowest. But he has not missed a Saturday since I met him, not one, not even the week his leash broke and he had no board. He borrowed mine. For seven years he has been the first one in the water and the last one out, and now he is going to Australia. Fair enough, really.
